nodes.label: Document Status System (current/planned/dormant/stub/superseded)

nodes.label: ContactRelay (packages/contact)
nodes.rationale: Renamed from ContactChannelAdapter during OKF port to match shipped code in packages/contact; the old heavyweight integrations table was replaced by the lean platform_channel_bindings concept

nodes.label: Taxonomy Curation Process (4-Phase Runbook)
nodes.rationale: 4-phase Document→Collate→Harmonize→Curate process ensures consistency; consumer search language preferred over formal taxonomy terms; noun form preferred over role names

nodes.label: Schwartz Basic Values (Values Source)
nodes.rationale: Schwartz academic labels mapped to friendlier user-facing terms (e.g., Benevolence → Helpfulness) to improve consumer accessibility

nodes.label: WhatsApp Groups API (Oct 2025)
nodes.rationale: 8-member group limit and 100K+ conversation threshold make official API impractical for most Personus community organizers; third-party providers recommended instead

nodes.label: Whapi.Cloud (Recommended WhatsApp Provider)
nodes.rationale: Best documentation, active development, and Communities API support (beta) among third-party WhatsApp providers; recommended over Maytapi and Wassenger

nodes.label: Telegram Mini Apps (Embedded Web Apps)
nodes.rationale: Most strategically important Telegram feature for Personus: enables embedding the full profile editor, search UI, and community dashboard inside Telegram with zero-friction auth via initData

nodes.label: grammY (Recommended Telegram Bot Framework)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript-first, modern middleware, excellent Next.js webhookCallback integration; preferred over Telegraf (complex types) and node-telegram-bot-api (no TypeScript)

nodes.label: Agentic Commerce Protocol & Commerce Personas Research
Commerce Persona
nodes.rationale: Same architecture as professional personas (master trait pool → selective projection → per-context sharing → consent management); commerce attributes are new trait categories added via trait_metadata rows

nodes.label: Profile (Master Trait Collection)
nodes.rationale: Profile is the investment (exhaustive, private, always growing); Persona is the payoff — mental model that drives user engagement and progressive revelation

nodes.label: Contact Preferences Model (GDPR-Inspired)
nodes.rationale: Replaces single contactPolicy enum with structured four-category consent model (discovery, contact, data sharing, communication) aligned with GDPR purpose-bound consent

nodes.label: Matrix Application Service API
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built for what Personus needs: observe community activity, create virtual users representing personas, facilitate introductions; requires homeserver admin access for registration

nodes.label: AT Protocol Privacy Gap (Public-Only Repos)
nodes.rationale: All AT Protocol data is public; conflicts with Personus per-persona visibility controls; mitigation is dual storage (public personas in atproto, private data in Neon DB)

nodes.label: Digital Identity Landscape & Integration Opportunities Research
Composable Trust Score (Human Passport Model)
nodes.rationale: Rather than picking a single verification provider, Personus aggregates optional trust signals (PoP, legal ID, professional creds, community endorsements, platform verification) — modeled on Human Passport stamp approach

nodes.label: Frugal PRD Shape (6-Section Convention)
nodes.rationale: Dense PRDs ship faster and stay maintained; 17-section canonical library template is too heavyweight — leads to prose duplication and drift; 6-section frugal shape targets ~150 lines per PRD

nodes.label: Product Area Decomposition Rubric (5 Rules)
nodes.rationale: Areas shaped by user value bundle (Rule 1) and architectural footprint (Rule 2); cross-cutting concerns excluded (Rule 3); future areas deferred to stub PRDs (Rule 4); 6-8 area target provides manageable scope (Rule 5)

nodes.label: Communities Domain PRD
nodes.rationale: Root PRD for the communities domain; pins 3 invariants and references all sub-specs and the guilds sub-PRD. EXTRACTED from frontmatter status field.

nodes.label: Membership Spec

nodes.label: Member Directory Spec

nodes.label: Invitations Spec
nodes.rationale: Invite links, codes, direct invitations, landing page, management table.

nodes.label: Activity and Analytics Spec
nodes.rationale: Activity feed, analytics dashboard, health score, member activation.

nodes.label: Moderation Spec

nodes.label: Notifications Spec
nodes.rationale: Notification events for community owners and members, delivery channels, preferences, weekly digest.

nodes.label: Integrations UI Spec
nodes.rationale: Reference doc mapping integration UI to integrations spec suite.

nodes.label: Notices Spec

nodes.label: Community Closure Spec

nodes.label: Community Relationships Spec

nodes.label: Monorepo Migration Spec
nodes.rationale: Turborepo migration, 5 shared packages (@personus/constants, types, db, validations, auth), admin app scaffold, 182 import rewrites.

nodes.label: Taxonomy Admin Spec
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy list/CRUD, value management, bulk import/export, audit trail (claims to define admin_audit_log), cache invalidation via webhook. Depends on 00-prd and 01-monorepo-migration.

nodes.label: System Settings Spec

nodes.rationale: Admin dashboard, user management, user detail tabs, impersonation (signed JWT 30min, assertNotImpersonating() guard), community management, audit log viewer. Depends on 00-prd + 01-monorepo-migration + 02-taxonomy-admin + 04-system-settings.

nodes.label: Community
nodes.rationale: Core data entity. Has communityType FK, parentCommunityId self-reference (DRIFT: planned to be replaced by community_relationships table per ADR #18), and vector(1536) embedding column for pgvector similarity search.

nodes.label: CommunityType
nodes.rationale: Enum with 9 values: club, guild, organization, friends, workplace, customer, neighborhood, event, educational. EXTRACTED from schema-spec.

nodes.label: CommunityMember
nodes.rationale: Three-part composite key (userId, personaId, communityId) — the membership invariant. Never collapse to two-part key. EXTRACTED from schema-spec.

nodes.label: GuildSkillCategory
nodes.rationale: Guild sub-entity defining skill categories offered by a guild community. FK to Community (guild type).

nodes.label: GuildMembershipTier
nodes.rationale: Guild sub-entity defining membership tiers (e.g. apprentice, journeyman, master). FK to Community (guild type).

nodes.label: GuildOffering
nodes.rationale: Guild sub-entity representing a service or product offered by the guild. FK to Community (guild type).

nodes.label: GuildOfferingMember
nodes.rationale: Junction entity linking CommunityMember to GuildOffering. FK to GuildOffering and CommunityMember.

nodes.label: GuildRequest
nodes.rationale: Guild sub-entity representing a member request for guild services. FK to Community (guild type) and CommunityMember.

nodes.label: Three-Part Membership Invariant
nodes.rationale: Core domain invariant: membership is always (userId, personaId, communityId). Never collapse to two-part key. Prevents persona leakage across communities. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Public Presence 3-Tier Model
nodes.rationale: Three tiers: private (invite-only, not discoverable), discoverable (appears in search, no public detail), full (full public page). Controls visibility in explore page and directory. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: CX Chat Integration
nodes.rationale: AI-powered customer experience chat embedded on community public pages and settings flows. EXTRACTED from spec.

nodes.label: Member Trait Schema
nodes.rationale: Per-community trait schema that extends the global trait taxonomy for community-specific member attributes. Inherited by child communities in chapter_of relationships. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Unmet Needs
nodes.rationale: Member-declared needs that have not been fulfilled by the community; surfaced in member directory for CX matching. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Capability Profile
nodes.rationale: Aggregated view of a member's skills, offerings, and traits as visible within a community directory. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Public Member Directory
nodes.rationale: Opt-in public listing of members with capability profiles, gated by community's public presence setting. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Community Embedding
nodes.rationale: pgvector vector(1536) column on Community table used for semantic similarity search of communities. Powers similar-communities recommendations. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: MCP Discovery Tools
nodes.rationale: Model Context Protocol tools exposed by Personus for AI agents to discover and query communities. Part of AIO (AI-Optimized Discovery) strategy. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: schema.org JSON-LD
nodes.rationale: Structured data markup on community public pages for SEO and AI crawler indexing. Part of AIO strategy. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Community Feed API
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable feed API for aggregating community listings, consumable by AI systems and partner integrations. Part of AIO strategy. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: llms.txt
nodes.rationale: llms.txt file at well-known URL providing AI-readable metadata about the platform and community listings. Part of AIO strategy. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Similar Communities
nodes.rationale: Recommendations for communities semantically similar to the current one, powered by pgvector cosine similarity on community embeddings. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Network Communities
nodes.rationale: Communities related via explicit relationship links (chapter_of, affiliated_with) surfaced in the explore/discovery page. INFERRED from spec context.

nodes.label: chapter_of Relationship
nodes.rationale: Community relationship type where one community is a local/regional chapter of a parent organization. Enables trait schema inheritance from parent. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: affiliated_with Relationship
nodes.rationale: Peer-level affiliation between communities with no hierarchy. Does not enable trait schema inheritance. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: referral_partner Relationship
nodes.rationale: Communities with a formal referral agreement; enables cross-community member recommendations. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: cohort_of Relationship
nodes.rationale: Time-bounded cohort community that is a subset of a parent community (e.g. cohort of an educational program). EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Trait Schema Inheritance
nodes.rationale: Mechanism by which child communities in chapter_of relationships inherit the parent community's trait schema extensions. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: 30-Day Closure Grace Period
nodes.rationale: After initiating a community close (hard delete path), a 30-day grace period allows members to export data before permanent deletion. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Community Health Score
nodes.rationale: Composite score derived from member activation, engagement, and growth metrics. Surfaced on analytics dashboard. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Turborepo
nodes.rationale: Build orchestration tool used for the Personus monorepo. Manages task pipelines across apps and shared packages. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Admin App
nodes.rationale: New admin application scaffolded as part of monorepo migration. Separate from consumer app. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Consumer App
nodes.rationale: Primary consumer-facing application in the monorepo. Underwent 182 import rewrites to use shared packages. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Shared Packages
nodes.rationale: Five shared packages created: @personus/constants, @personus/types, @personus/db, @personus/validations, @personus/auth. Used by both apps. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Trait Taxonomies Table
nodes.rationale: DB table storing 62 trait categories and ~1054 trait values. Admin UI provides CRUD, bulk import/export, and cache invalidation via webhook. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Admin Audit Log Table
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS: 02-taxonomy-admin.md §5 defines admin_audit_log for taxonomy changes; 04-system-settings.md §5 says admin_audit_log is defined in 05-user-and-community-ops.md. Likely a single shared table but ownership is disputed across specs.

nodes.label: system_settings Table
nodes.rationale: DB table storing 30 initial platform settings across 6 categories: rate_limits, ai, features, cache, import, defaults. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: getSetting() Function
nodes.rationale: Read-only API for consuming platform settings. Backed by in-memory Map cache to avoid per-request DB hits. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Feature Flags
nodes.rationale: Feature toggle settings stored in the features category of system_settings. Consumed via getSetting(). INFERRED from spec structure.

nodes.label: Admin Impersonation
nodes.rationale: Read-only admin impersonation using short-lived signed JWT (30 min TTL). Not using Clerk sessions. assertNotImpersonating() guard prevents writes. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Audit Log Viewer
nodes.rationale: Admin UI for viewing admin_audit_log entries. Reads from the audit log table whose ownership is AMBIGUOUS between 02-taxonomy-admin and 05-user-and-community-ops.

nodes.label: User Management
nodes.rationale: Admin dashboard feature for viewing/managing platform users, including user detail tabs (profile, communities, activity). EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Admin Community Management
nodes.rationale: Admin-side community management distinct from community-owner moderation (07-moderation.md). Covers platform-level interventions. EXTRACTED.

nodes.label: Platform Ops Admin App (admin.personus.ai)
nodes.rationale: Control plane for internal operators; manages taxonomy, trait metadata, system settings, and user/community ops — distinct from the developer-facing Next.js app; live at admin.personus.ai

nodes.label: Admin vs Developer Boundary (Values vs Structure)
nodes.rationale: Admin app owns values (what traits mean, completeness weights, live settings); developer tooling owns structure (schema migrations, code). Prevents values-as-code anti-pattern.

nodes.label: Trait Metadata Admin UI (Safe-Property Editor)
nodes.rationale: Admin UI edits only safe properties (display label, completeness weight, placeholder text, icon, display order) — schema-changing properties (DB column type, validation) require developer migration

nodes.label: Persona Coach AI Agent
nodes.rationale: Guides users through profile completion and persona curation; operates with cost caps and identity isolation via Mastra RequestContext

nodes.label: AI Coach Cost Caps (per-request / per-user-daily / per-agent-run)
nodes.rationale: Hard guardrails: per-request ≤$0.50, per-user-daily ≤$10, per-agent-run ≤$5; enforced at the Mastra agent layer before any LLM call

nodes.label: Trust-Backed Capability Match (Discovery Core Deliverable)
nodes.rationale: A capability match is trust-backed when it combines semantic similarity (pgvector cosine) with community endorsement weight; this distinction is what differentiates Personus from keyword search

nodes.label: Discovery North Star: Trust-Backed Matches per Week
Discovery MCP Endpoint (External AI Agent Queries)
Platform Channel Integration Tier Framework (1-5)
nodes.rationale: Five-tier capability model: Tier 1 Link, Tier 2 Notify, Tier 3 Interact, Tier 4 Sync, Tier 5 Embed. Governs which platforms get which investment level; not all platforms reach Tier 5.

nodes.label: externalPlatforms JSONB (Layer 1 Community Link)
nodes.rationale: Lean JSONB field on communities table; stores external platform URL/ID for Tier 1 link-only integrations; no separate table needed at this tier

nodes.label: platform_channel_bindings Table (Layer 2 Operational Records)
nodes.rationale: Lean replacement for the heavyweight integrations table; stores per-community per-platform operational state (bot token hash, webhook URL, enabled tiers); one row per (communityId, platformKey)

nodes.label: WhatsApp Integration (Tier 1 Link; Meta API constraints)
nodes.rationale: Meta banned general WhatsApp chatbots Jan 2026; Personus uses link-only Tier 1 now; WhatsApp Flows (task-specific mini-apps) are the approved expansion path

nodes.label: Signal Integration (Tier 1 Link-Only by Design)
nodes.rationale: Signal intentionally has no public bot API; Tier 1 link-only is the correct scope — storing the group invite link on the community record so members can find the Signal group

nodes.label: Telegram Mini Apps (Tier 5 Embedded UI via initData Auth)
nodes.rationale: Next.js pages served inside Telegram with zero-friction auth via initData HMAC verification; enables full profile editor and community dashboard inside Telegram client

nodes.label: Bot Architecture: One Brain, Many Mouths
nodes.rationale: Single Mastra agent brain answers across all platforms; platform adapters are thin I/O shims; identity resolution (asAgent()) unifies the persona context before the LLM sees any message

nodes.label: Mastra Channels Framework (Adopted 2026-05-11; v1.26)
nodes.rationale: Auto-generates webhooks, owns DM/mention/thread routing, dedup, and per-thread memory; replaces hand-rolled webhook scaffolding; adopted because it matches the Personus one-brain-many-mouths model

nodes.label: Fly.io Persistent Process (Matrix Appservice Host)
nodes.rationale: Matrix Appservice requires a persistent TCP listener — incompatible with serverless Next.js. Fly.io provides the always-on process; Discord Gateway similarly needs persistent connection.

nodes.label: asAgent() Principal Delegation (PER-5/PER-6/PER-17 Prerequisite)
nodes.rationale: Bot actions must be scoped to the community persona, not a system-wide principal. asAgent() resolves the Mastra RequestContext principal from the incoming platform event before calling any service layer.

nodes.label: Aggregated Anonymized Capability Announcements (Fediverse Differentiator)
nodes.rationale: Publishing anonymized aggregate capability signals (e.g., '3 Python engineers available') to the fediverse is the unique Personus differentiator vs generic ActivityPub presence — drives cross-community capability discovery

nodes.label: Sparks Generosity Engine (Dormant Pre-PMF; No Code Exists)
nodes.rationale: Intentionally parked before product-market fit; Sparks credit system rewards endorsements and profile completion but risks gaming; PRD preserved for future activation with no active Linear tickets

nodes.label: Shadow Persona (Placeholder for Non-User; shadow_personas Table)
nodes.rationale: Primary viral growth mechanism: when a community member endorses someone not yet on Personus, a shadow persona is created. The shadow persona is visible in the directory and drives an invitation to claim.

nodes.label: Atomic Endorsement Transfer on Shadow Claim
nodes.rationale: On claim: shadow persona merged into new real persona, all endorsements atomically transferred in a single transaction, shadow record soft-deleted. Ensures no endorsement loss during claim.

nodes.label: Persona Unlinkability Principle (No Auto-Link for Same User)
nodes.rationale: Two personas owned by the same User must never be automatically linkable — only opt-in explicit linking is permitted. Enforced at the service layer and tested in gates.ts.

nodes.label: trait_metadata Table (41 Rows; Drives Consumer UI)
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for how every trait type is displayed and edited; 41 rows cover all current trait types; displayConfig + editConfig columns drive the entire rendering system with zero hardcoded components

nodes.label: Commerce Privacy Tier (5-Level: public→selective→gated→sensitive→agent_local)
nodes.rationale: Governs trait visibility in commerce contexts; agent_local means the trait is visible only to the user's own AI agents, never to external parties or LLMs directly

nodes.label: UserTraits (Master Trait Pool — Exactly 1 per User)
nodes.rationale: A single UserTraits record holds the exhaustive trait pool for one user; personas project a selective lens over it. This copy-not-reference invariant ensures trait edits are persona-local.

nodes.label: Endorsement Entity (Positive-Only, Community-Scoped, Persona-Identified)
nodes.rationale: Endorsements are identified by persona not by user — preserving unlinkability. Positive-only (no down-votes). Community-scoped (an endorsement in one community does not appear in another).

nodes.label: ContactRelay Service (packages/contact; Distinct from PlatformChannels and NotificationTransport)
nodes.rationale: ContactRelay (packages/contact) handles private mediated contact between personas. It is architecturally distinct from PlatformChannels (Mastra bots) and NotificationTransport (in-app/email notices). Never conflate these three channel concepts.

nodes.label: Personas PRD
nodes.description: Umbrella PRD for all persona features: master trait pool, lifecycle, visibility, layout, public pages, shadow personas, endorsements, contact requests. Three Pins: traits copied never referenced, no PII in personas, every public persona is AI-queryable and claimable.

nodes.label: Persona Creation Wizard
nodes.description: 3-step wizard: type selection → basics (displayName, headline, layout preset) → coach redirect. Components: layout-preset-picker.tsx, avatar-initial-editor.tsx. Server action: createPersona().

nodes.label: Persona List with Placeholder Cards
nodes.description: Persona grid with placeholder cards for empty slots; PERSONA_PLACEHOLDERS config with professional and personal presets; persona-card.tsx compact and full variants.

nodes.label: Persona Deletion Cascade
nodes.description: 10-step transaction: soft-delete endorsements, community memberships, contact requests, shadow personas, then hard-delete persona. getPersonaDeletionImpact() previews cascade.

nodes.label: Persona Completeness Score
nodes.description: 0-100 score across 9 weighted dimensions; recalculated on updatePersonaTraits(); stored on personas.completenessScore; drives AI coach suggestions.

nodes.label: User Profile View
nodes.description: /profile route showing master trait pool with quick-add bar; classification engine auto-classifies new traits; server actions: getUserTraits(), classifyAndAdd(), addTrait(), updateTrait(), removeTrait().

nodes.label: Trait Classification Engine
nodes.description: 3-tier pipeline in lib/profile/classify.ts: Tier 1 taxonomy match (<50ms), Tier 2 pattern match (<50ms), Tier 3 LLM fallback via gpt-4o-mini structured output (~500ms).

nodes.label: LinkedIn ZIP Import
nodes.description: Privacy-first: ZIP parsed client-side via fflate+papaparse. PII files silently skipped. Parses Positions, Education, Skills, Certifications, Languages, Profile CSVs. Raw data never leaves browser.

nodes.label: URL Import via AI Extraction
nodes.description: Jina Reader API (r.jina.ai) scrapes page to markdown; gpt-4o-mini generateObject() extracts structured traits. URL type detection adapts extraction strategy. Rate-limited: 10/hour, 50/day per user. Cost: $0.001-0.005/scrape.

nodes.label: Trait Divergence Badge
nodes.description: trait-divergence-badge.tsx detects mismatch between persona.traits JSONB snapshot and current UserTraits version; prompts owner to sync.

nodes.label: Persona Visibility Tiers
nodes.description: 4-tier hierarchy: public → authenticated → community → private. VISIBILITY_RANK: {public:0, authenticated:1, community:2, private:3}. Each tier is a subset of level above. canViewPersona() in lib/auth/permissions.ts, getViewablePersona() in app/actions/personas.ts.

nodes.label: Per-Trait Visibility Overrides
nodes.description: Per-trait visibility stored in traits JSONB as visibilityOverride field. Can only restrict, never widen beyond persona-level visibility. filterTraitsByViewerVisibility() in lib/personas/trait-visibility.ts.

nodes.label: MCP Exposure Settings
nodes.description: mcpEnabled (per-persona toggle), mcpTraitVisibility (per-trait JSONB map), mcpPreferences (user-level: searchMatching, introductions, directMessages). COMMERCE_AGENT_LOCAL_KEYS never exposed in MCP responses. lib/mcp/tools.ts: getEffectiveTraitVisibility(), filterTraitsByVisibility().

nodes.label: Contact Preferences
nodes.description: 4 GDPR-inspired categories: discovery (searchVisibility, aiMatching, endorsementVisibility), contact (directMessages, connectionRequests, opportunityContact), dataSharing (analyticsContribution), communication (activityNotifications, coachNudges). Stored as personas.contactPreferences JSONB. checkContactAuthorization() in lib/auth/permissions.ts.

nodes.label: Layout Presets
nodes.description: 5 presets + auto: professional (person default), personal, community (org default), service, creative. Each defines heroElements[], sectionOrder[], endorsementStyle (cards/inline/count-only/testimonial-carousel), ctaLabel, ctaStyle, density.

nodes.label: Persona Theme System
nodes.description: PersonaTheme interface: colorPalette (7 options: default/ocean/forest/sunset/midnight/lavender/earth), headerTreatment (4: gradient/solid/minimal/image), density (3: compact/comfortable/airy), accentColor, headerImageUrl. personas.theme JSONB default '{}'.

nodes.label: Layout Config Resolver
nodes.description: resolveLayoutPreset() at lib/personas/layout-config.ts:240 handles 'auto' resolution to Professional (person) or Community (org). getLayoutConfig() at line 249 merges preset defaults with persona.theme JSONB overrides.

nodes.label: Layout Preset Picker
nodes.description: layout-preset-picker.tsx with compact mode for creation wizard; shows 5 preset options with entity-type suggestion highlighting; used in both creation wizard and edit flows.

nodes.label: Public Persona Page
nodes.description: /p/[uri] server-rendered page; zero client-side data fetching; visitor action bar (Endorse, Request Introduction, Share); community context via ?community= query param; private personas return 404.

nodes.label: Persona SEO Metadata
nodes.description: buildPersonaDescription(), buildOpenGraphMetadata(), buildRobotsDirective() in lib/personas/seo.ts. Robots directive respects visibility: public=index, private/authenticated=noindex. Title: '{DisplayName} -- Personus'.

nodes.label: JSON-LD Structured Data
nodes.description: buildPersonJsonLd(), buildOrganizationJsonLd() in lib/personas/structured-data.ts. Maps to schema.org Person/Organization with hasOccupation, alumniOf, hasCredential, knowsAbout, interactionStatistic, makesOffer, seeks.

nodes.label: AIO Optimization
nodes.description: AI-Indexing Optimization: buildAIDescription() up to 500 chars; semantic HTML with article/section/aria-label structure for AI crawlers (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude web search).

nodes.label: OG Image Generation
nodes.description: GET /api/og/persona/[uri] returns 1200x630 PNG via Next.js ImageResponse/Satori. getOgPaletteColors() maps 7 palettes to hex values. Cache-Control: s-maxage=86400. Private personas return 404.

nodes.label: Visitor Actions Bar
nodes.description: visitor-action-bar.tsx: Endorse (link to /endorse/{uri}, no auth), Request Introduction (auth required, redirects to sign-in if not), Share (SharePersonaDialog with clipboard + Web Share API). Mobile: sticky bottom bar.

nodes.label: Section-Level Editing Pattern
nodes.description: LinkedIn-style: read-only view with pencil icons per section; tapping opens focused editor for that section only; each section saves independently. Single edit page rejected as too complex for heterogeneous trait shapes.

nodes.label: Explicit Save Behavior
nodes.description: Explicit save always (no auto-save for identity data). 'Save' for section editors, 'Done' for simple pickers. Spinner + 'Saving...' during save. Toast via sonner on success: '[Section] saved'.

nodes.label: Unsaved Changes Dialog
nodes.description: unsaved-changes-dialog.tsx: shown when user navigates away with unsaved changes. Verb-based labels: 'Discard Changes' / 'Keep Editing' (not Yes/No). No dialog if no changes made.

nodes.label: Mobile Editing UX
nodes.description: Full-screen editors on mobile (no modals/popovers for primary editing). Bottom sheets only for secondary actions. 44x44pt touch targets. No multi-column forms below 768px. Character counters for constrained fields.

nodes.label: User Entity
nodes.description: users table: clerkUserId (unique, immutable), did (optional AT Protocol DID), defaultContactPreferences JSONB, mcpPreferences JSONB. One per human. Clerk is primary auth.

nodes.label: UserTraits Entity
nodes.description: user_traits table: one-per-user, traits JSONB (PII-scanned before write, GIN-indexed for search). Master trait pool. Never read directly by public surfaces. Source for persona trait snapshots.

nodes.label: TraitMetadata Entity
nodes.description: trait_metadata table: key (immutable string), category enum, dataType enum, displayConfig JSON (type: tag_list/timeline/pill_list/card_list), editConfig JSON, isSearchable bool, isEndorsable bool, privacyTier. 41 seed rows across 5 categories.

nodes.label: TraitTaxonomy Entity
nodes.description: trait_taxonomies table: suggested values per trait key. Unique constraint on (traitKey, taxonomySlug). 10 taxonomy files covering skills, qualities, values, interests, etc.

nodes.label: Persona Entity
nodes.description: personas table: uri (immutable slug), entityType enum, visibility enum, traits JSONB (snapshot copy from UserTraits), mcpEnabled bool, mcpTraitVisibility JSONB, embedding vector[1536] (ivfflat cosine), layoutPreset (default 'auto'), theme JSONB (default '{}'), contactPreferences JSONB, completenessScore int.

nodes.label: ShadowPersona Entity
nodes.description: shadow_personas table: communityId required, createdByPersonaUri (persona not userId — unlinkability), claimToken (secure random), claimStatus enum (unclaimed/claimed/expired), embedding vector[1536], expiresAt (default 90 days).

nodes.label: Endorsement Entity
nodes.description: endorsements table: fromPersonaUri (persona not userId), XOR(toPersonaUri, toShadowPersonaId), communityId required, positive-only (no negative endorsements), active bool for soft-revoke, testimonial text, strength enum.

nodes.label: ContactRequest Entity
nodes.description: contact_requests table: raw contact details never stored (contact channel indirection). Three sender modes: persona, agent, anonymous. Status lifecycle: pending/accepted/rejected/expired. triageNote and triageScore from AI mediation.

nodes.label: Unlinkability Invariant
nodes.description: Personas never reveal they share the same User. ShadowPersona uses createdByPersonaUri not userId. Endorsements use fromPersonaUri not userId. Cross-persona connections only via community-scoped opt-in linking.

nodes.label: Trait Copy Not Reference
nodes.description: persona.traits is a JSONB snapshot copied from UserTraits at save time. Deleting a persona does not affect the user's master traits or other personas. Divergence is detected and surfaced via trait-divergence-badge.tsx.

nodes.label: Apple Music Consumer UX Patterns
nodes.description: Key patterns for Personus dashboard: hero section first, section-based vertical scroll, mixed card sizes (2 full + 1 partial peek), calm focus density, algo-torial personalization, productive friction onboarding, implicit contextual prompts (assertions not questions).

nodes.label: Liquid Glass Design System
nodes.description: iOS 26 Liquid Glass: translucent refractive surfaces. Design token alignment: OKLCH colors, Fraunces+Outfit fonts, shadcn/ui with backdrop-blur, Framer Motion animations.

nodes.label: Consumer UX Philosophy
nodes.description: 'Does this make the user feel seen, or filed?' 10 transformational shifts: data-first→emotion-first, functional→personality, form→identity. Avoids internal jargon (no 'shadow persona', 'entity type' shown to users).

nodes.label: Personus Design Tokens
nodes.description: Typography: Fraunces (display headers), Outfit (body). Spacing: 32-48px section gaps. Cards: 16-20px corner radius, soft diffused shadows. Rotating hero prompt: 7 priority states with accent colors.

nodes.label: SoundCloud UX Patterns
nodes.description: Strip vanity metrics; waveform as multi-purpose element; peek pattern (2 full + 1 partial). Applied to Personus persona card layout and dashboard density decisions.

nodes.label: Metadata-Driven Rendering
nodes.description: TraitSection reads displayConfig from trait_metadata DB rows; renders via tag-list/timeline/pill-list/card-list. New trait types added via DB insert with no code deploy. TraitEditor similarly driven by editConfig.

nodes.label: Privacy Tier Badge Component
nodes.description: 5-tier badge: public (green globe), selective (blue toggle), gated (amber lock), sensitive (red shield), agent_local (purple bot). Reads displayConfig.privacyTier from TraitMetadata. Rendered alongside trait display name in both display and edit modes.

nodes.label: Commerce Trait Metadata Examples
nodes.description: fitPreference (string/select), shippingPreferences (object/card_list/selective), budgetPreferences (object/card_list/agent_local — never shared via MCP). Demonstrate metadata-driven rendering for commerce category.

nodes.label: next-intl Internationalization
nodes.description: next-intl v4 for all user-facing strings in apps/web. English only for first 6 months. useTranslations/getTranslations hooks. messages/en.json namespaced by feature area. createNextIntlPlugin() in next.config.ts.

nodes.label: Profile Page Attention Hierarchy
nodes.description: Eye-tracking: F-pattern (text-heavy profiles like LinkedIn), Z-pattern (visual/sparse like Instagram), Gutenberg (balanced layouts). Priority: Photo → Name+Title → Trust Badge/Rating → Primary CTA → One-line description → Key metrics → Content grid. Top 300-400px gets 80%+ of attention.

nodes.label: Trust Signal Patterns by Category
nodes.description: Professional: title+company affiliation. Marketplace/freelance: star rating+review count+platform badges. Personal/social: follower count+verification. Community: member count+activity+mutual members. Service: star rating+review volume+background checks. Creative: portfolio quality+engagement.

nodes.label: Profile Design Recommendations for Personus
nodes.description: Endorsements in hero zone (like Upwork Job Success Score, not buried like LinkedIn). CTA is 'Contact' (mediated) not 'Connect' (social). Tag-pill pattern for skills. Org personas borrow from community/group playbook. Shadow personas: Linktree simplicity. Endorsement should show relationship context.

nodes.label: Communities Build Status Snapshot 2026-02-23
nodes.description: Fully built: DB schema, 9 community types seed, guild tables (5), createCommunity action, community wizard, CASL authz. Partially built: explore page, admin dashboard, public page, member management, analytics. Gap list of 18 missing features.

nodes.label: Communities Implementation Wave Priorities
nodes.description: Wave 1 (core): lifecycle+membership+directory. Wave 2 (growth): discovery+invitations+notices. Wave 3 (ops): analytics+moderation+notifications+integrations-ui+closure+relationships. Dependency: 01→02→03 core loop.

nodes.label: Legacy Documentation Index
nodes.description: Legacy hand-written nav index superseded by generated index.md. Covers Foundation, Specs (Personas/Communities/Integrations/Platform Ops/Discovery/AI Coaches/Commerce/Sparks), Patterns, Business Model, Decisions, Research, Guides.

nodes.label: Agent Network Overview (v5)
nodes.description: 3 access modes: public web (SEO/JSON-LD endpoints), MCP server (anonymous/authenticated/enterprise tiers), workspace integrations (Slack/Discord group-backed). Agents: NLP Gateway (router), Query Planner, Trust Graph Agent, Value Conveyance, Result Assembler.

nodes.label: Persona Coach Agent (v5)
nodes.description: gpt-4o voice-first agent (tts-1-hd nova / whisper-1). 7-turn conversation arc (~5 min, target 85-88% completeness). Adapts for person vs. org. PII guardrails via checkPIITool. Tools: updatePersonaFieldTool, getGroupSchemaTool, getCompletenessTool.

nodes.label: Recommender Coach Agent (v5)
nodes.description: Lightweight flow: shadow persona + endorsement in ~30 seconds via quick one-liner. Enrichment flow optional. Batch mode for multiple recommendations. Tools: createShadowPersonaTool, enrichShadowPersonaTool, createEndorsementTool, sendClaimInviteTool.

nodes.label: Contact Mediation Agent (v5)
nodes.description: gpt-4o-mini; generates: triage note (2-3 sentences), triage score (0-100), matched openTo fields, trust chain ('Requester → [Person A] → You'). Runs on each inbound ContactRequest.

nodes.label: MCP Tool Definitions (v5)
nodes.description: 5 tools: personus_search (query, entityType, scope, groupIds, location, maxResults), personus_request_introduction, personus_get_persona, personus_list_groups, personus_get_affiliations. 3 tiers: anonymous (10 req/min), authenticated (100/min), enterprise (1000/min).

nodes.label: Workspace Integrations (v5)
nodes.description: Slack (Bolt SDK, Block Kit) and Discord (discord.js, rich embeds) group-backed bots. Commands: /personus find, /personus directory, /personus profile. Optional workspace member sync. PlatformIntegration entity links workspace to Personus group.

nodes.label: Communities PRD Vision (2026-02-23)
nodes.description: Communities as 'intelligence layers' and 'multiplier': makes hidden group capabilities visible. CO (Community Organizer) creates/stewards; CM (Community Member) joins and gets discovered. 12 feature specs (01-12). User journeys: CO launch, CM join, CO manage, visitor discover, public directory.

nodes.label: Nine Community Types (2026-02-23)
nodes.description: Club, Organization, Friends, Guild, Workplace, Customer, Neighborhood, Event, Educational. Each defines communityTraitSchema, memberTraitSchema, featureFlags (events/chapters/skill_taxonomy/request_routing/offerings/membership_tiers), join policy defaults.

nodes.label: Personas PRD Core Thesis (2026-02-23)
nodes.description: 'You are not one thing' — two-layer model: user traits (master) → personas (published views). 9 decisions: hybrid JSONB, traits copy not reference, metadata-driven rendering, 5 layout presets, completeness scoring (9 dimensions), auto-resolve from entity type, community-scoped shadow personas, embeddings from structured trait text, URI-based identification.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Persona Model (2026-02-23)
nodes.description: Base (displayName, headline, location, entityType) + Attribute (personas.traits JSONB snapshot) + Context (community_members.memberTraits, community-specific). Context layer defined per-community by memberTraitSchema.

nodes.label: Product Area Inventory (2026-04-13)
nodes.description: 8 product areas: Personas (partial, 11 built+6 planned), Communities (partial, 9+8), Discovery (candidate, no PRD), AI Coaches (candidate, no PRD), Integrations (partial, 0 built), Commerce (dormant), Sparks (dormant), Platform Ops (partial). nodes.label: Discovery Area Definition (2026-04-13)
nodes.description: Discovery delivers trust-backed matches to capability queries via semantic search over personas/shadows/communities. nodes.label: Commerce Area Definition (2026-04-13)
nodes.description: Commerce (dormant): users control what AI agents disclose during transactions via commerce personas with per-category consent, ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol), privacy-preserving payment scoping. Fully designed, zero code.

nodes.label: Product Area Decomposition Discipline (2026-04-13)

nodes.label: Authentication Validation Spec (2026-04-12)
nodes.description: 4 auth methods: phone SMS (Clerk), Apple Sign-In (Clerk), Google Sign-In (Clerk), Bluesky AT Protocol OAuth (additive identity link, not replacement for Clerk). User model additions: phone, atprotoHandle, atprotoTokens JSONB (AES-256-GCM encrypted), authMethods text[].

nodes.label: AT Protocol OAuth Flow (2026-04-12)
nodes.description: PDS-based authorization: handle → DID → PDS → PAR → redirect → callback → token exchange. DPoP (RFC 9449) required: @atproto/oauth-client-node handles complexity. Client metadata at /.well-known/oauth-client-metadata. Scopes: atproto + transition:generic. Clerk owns session; AT Protocol tokens stored server-side.

nodes.label: Users table
nodes.description: Core users table: identity anchor, links to Clerk auth, roots all trait and persona ownership

nodes.label: Personas table
nodes.description: Personas table: purpose-specific identity slices with vector(1536) embedding column, visibility level, layout_preset, theme JSONB, and persona URI. Central entity in the data model.

nodes.label: Trait system (user_traits + trait_metadata + trait_taxonomies)
nodes.description: Master attribute pool: user_traits holds raw values; trait_metadata drives rendering; trait_taxonomies provides controlled vocabulary. Metadata-driven rendering pattern.

nodes.label: Communities table (9 community types)
nodes.description: Unified communities table using communityType discriminator. 9 types: Club, Organization, Friends, Guild, Workplace, Customer, Neighborhood, Event, Educational — seeded via community_types table.

nodes.label: Shadow personas table
nodes.description: PII-free representations of non-users created by existing users. Claimable via token. Support the growth flywheel: recommend a non-user → shadow created → shadow discovered → claim invite sent.

nodes.label: Endorsements table (trust graph edges)
nodes.description: Directed trust graph edges between personas. Each endorsement is typed by relationship and skill, forming a queryable trust chain used in search scoring and Pathfinder trust-chain visualization.

nodes.label: Vector embeddings (pgvector, 1536 dims, ivfflat)
nodes.description: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) stored in personas.embedding via pgvector ivfflat index. Enables semantic search and trust-weighted ranked retrieval.

nodes.label: Commerce traits (28 traits, 8 categories, privacy tiers)
nodes.description: 28 commerce-specific traits in 8 categories with 5-tier privacy (public/selective/gated/sensitive/agent_local). Aligns with Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP, AP2) identity requirements.

nodes.label: Hybrid JSONB + relational architecture decision
nodes.description: Not pure 3NF, not pure document store. Community context stored in memberTraits JSONB (Context Layer); core trait values normalized. Balances schema flexibility with query performance.

nodes.label: CASL authorization engine
nodes.description: @casl/ability: chosen for embedded ABAC via MongoDB conditions, isomorphic TypeScript, 950K+/week downloads. Defines abilities per principal; model: rbac-with-ownership.

nodes.label: 6-layer authorization evaluation model
nodes.description: Six evaluation layers: network (public/private), persona visibility, trait disclosure, community membership, endorsement graph, AI agent tier. Applied in sequence to every request.

nodes.label: Persona visibility levels
nodes.description: Four visibility levels on each persona: public, authenticated, community, private. Structural trait disclosure — visibility applies to all traits in a persona, not per-trait flags.

nodes.label: MCP access tiers (anonymous / authenticated / enterprise)
nodes.description: Three-tier MCP access model: anonymous agents (public data only), authenticated agents (user-consented data), enterprise agents (negotiated data sharing agreements).

nodes.label: Shadow persona ownership lifecycle
nodes.description: State machine: created-by-endorser → discoverable-by-agents → claim-invite-sent → claimed-by-target-user → merged-with-real-account. Endorser loses ownership on claim.

nodes.label: GraphQL API (Pothos)
nodes.description: GraphQL schema built with Pothos code-first builder. Covers personas, communities, endorsements, contact requests, guild queries. Also exposes REST endpoints and OG image endpoints.

nodes.label: MCP endpoint and tool suite
nodes.description: 6 MCP tools including personus_search_people, personus_get_persona, personus_create_contact_request, personus_get_commerce_persona. Exposed at /api/mcp via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.

nodes.label: Technology stack
nodes.description: Next.js App Router + Vercel + Neon Postgres + pgvector + Drizzle ORM + Turborepo + Bun. Mastra 1.2 agents, Clerk auth, CASL authz, shadcn/ui + Tailwind v4, Vitest.

nodes.label: MVP phases (3 phases)
nodes.description: Three MVP delivery phases defined in the deployment spec. Also defines testing strategy (unit/integration/e2e), seed data approach, and Vercel deployment configuration.

nodes.label: Public web discovery (JSON-LD, Schema.org)
nodes.description: Public persona pages expose Schema.org JSON-LD for web crawler indexing. AI agents can discover Personus personas via standard web discovery before using the MCP endpoint.

nodes.label: Slack / Discord workspace integrations
nodes.description: Bot integrations for Slack and Discord workspaces. Allow community members to query personas and trigger introductions from within their existing workspace.

nodes.label: Persona Coach agent (Mastra)
nodes.description: Mastra agent that guides users through persona construction and optimization. Has tools: update_persona_field, get_persona, suggest_traits. Acts on behalf of authenticated User principal.

nodes.label: Community Coach agent (Mastra)
nodes.description: Mastra agent for community organizers. Provides member discovery, engagement analytics, and steward decision support within a community context.

nodes.label: Commerce Coach agent (Mastra)
nodes.description: Mastra agent that helps users build and optimize commerce personas aligned with ACP/AP2/UCP protocols. Surfaces offering opportunities and pricing recommendations.

nodes.label: Guild Routing Agent (Mastra tool: guild_route_request)
nodes.description: Mastra tool that routes incoming guild requests to matching members based on skill taxonomy and routing mode (auto/steward-reviewed/round-robin/broadcast).

nodes.label: Contact Mediation Agent
nodes.description: Mastra agent that mediates introduction requests: checks contact preferences, enforces GDPR consent categories, routes to correct persona, logs for audit. Ensures no PII is exposed without consent.

nodes.label: Recommender Coach / Discovery Agent (Mastra)
nodes.description: Dual-mode Mastra agent: RecommenderCoach assists users in finding and recommending people; DiscoveryAgent handles semantic search over pgvector embeddings for external queries.

nodes.label: DID-based identity anchor (AT Protocol)
nodes.description: Every Personus user is anchored to an AT Protocol DID (Decentralized Identifier). DID is the portable identity root that survives platform migration and enables dual storage.

nodes.label: Personus AT Protocol lexicons (ai.personus.*)
nodes.description: Custom AT Protocol record types: ai.personus.actor.profile, ai.personus.persona.record, ai.personus.trait.entry, ai.personus.endorsement.record, ai.personus.contact.request.

nodes.label: Dual storage model (Neon + AT Protocol repo)
nodes.description: Primary storage in Neon Postgres for query performance; AT Protocol Personal Data Server (PDS) for portability and decentralized ownership. Sync is async with Neon as source of truth.

nodes.label: Commerce protocol alignment (ACP, AP2, UCP)
nodes.description: Commerce personas are designed as identity layers for Agentic Commerce Protocol (OpenAI/Stripe), AP2 (Google), and Universal Commerce Protocol. Lexicons encode capability attestations agents can verify.

nodes.label: Bluesky / Atmosphere ecosystem (~40M users)
nodes.description: Bluesky social network (~40M users) built on AT Protocol. The Atmosphere ecosystem of apps shares the same DID namespace. Personus occupies the professional identity gap that Bluesky does not fill.

nodes.label: Atmosphere integration flywheel model
nodes.description: 4-phase integration roadmap: (A) DID anchoring, (B) public persona records, (C) federated endorsement graph, (D) cross-app discovery. Each phase grows Personus presence in the Atmosphere ecosystem.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Schema (Base / Attribute / Context)
nodes.description: Base Layer: universal traits (name, bio, skills). Attribute Layer: self-declared domain traits. Context Layer: community-specific overrides stored in memberTraits JSONB. Enables the profile-is-master / personas-are-lenses principle.

nodes.label: Persona completeness algorithm
nodes.description: Weighted scoring algorithm that computes persona completeness 0-100%. Drives the CompletenessIndicator UI component and Persona Coach suggestions. Sparks bonus triggered at 80%+.

nodes.label: Trust-weighted search scoring
nodes.description: Search ranking combines cosine similarity on pgvector embeddings with endorsement graph depth and endorsement quality signals. Pathfinder tier gets full trust-chain depth access.

nodes.label: Vision: personal agency in the agentic era
nodes.description: Core vision: Personus is a personal data control plane. Users control what gets shared, with whom, and under what terms — even as AI agents act on their behalf. Enabling personal agency in the agentic era.

nodes.label: Three interconnected use cases
nodes.description: People Discovery (find skilled people via trust-backed AI), Commerce Agency (service providers discoverable without paying for leads), Open Social Web (AT Protocol portability and Atmosphere participation).

nodes.label: 20 Foundational Principles
nodes.description: 20 non-negotiable principles including: no-PII-in-personas, masked contactability, addressable endpoints, dual-query (semantic+structured), AI-native, trust through endorsements, profile-is-everything/personas-are-lenses, GDPR consent, open social web.

nodes.label: Progressive onboarding (4 phases)
nodes.description: Phase 1: Be Found (minimal viable persona). Phase 2: Build Trust (endorsements, completeness). Phase 3: Join & Discover (communities, search). Phase 4: Create & Lead (guilds, commerce personas).

nodes.label: Shadow persona concept
nodes.description: PII-free proxy created when any user endorses or recommends a non-user. Discoverable by AI agents. Core growth mechanic: non-users become part of the network before joining.

nodes.label: Guilds (skill-centric communities)
nodes.description: Guilds are communities with communityType='guild' plus a backing organization persona. Add skill taxonomy, membership tiers, offerings catalog, and request routing on top of base community infrastructure.

nodes.label: Guild membership tiers (criteria + permissions JSONB)
nodes.description: guild_membership_tiers table: each tier has criteria JSONB (skill requirements, endorsement count) and permissions JSONB (routing eligibility, offering access). Up to 3 tiers on CO Base, unlimited on CO Pro.

nodes.label: Guild request routing modes
nodes.description: routingMode options: auto (AI-matched), steward-reviewed (human approval), round-robin (sequential), broadcast (all eligible members). CO Base: broadcast only. CO Pro: all 4 modes.

nodes.label: Guild offerings catalog
nodes.description: guild_offerings table: services/products guild members offer collectively. Linked to guild_offering_members. Platform fee on fulfillment: 5% on CO Base, 3% on CO Pro.

nodes.label: Guild membership as AT Protocol verifiable credential
nodes.description: Phase 3+ roadmap: guild membership tiers become portable verifiable credentials on the AT Protocol. Federated guild directories allow cross-platform skill discovery.

nodes.label: Persona layout presets (5 presets)
nodes.description: Five named layout presets: Professional, Personal, Community, Service, Creative. Each defines heroLayout, sectionOrder, heroMetrics, ctaLabel, ctaStyle, density, endorsementStyle, skillDisplay.

nodes.label: Visual theme system (7 palettes, 4 headers, 3 densities)
nodes.description: Theme system: 7 color palettes (OKLCH), 4 header treatments, 3 density levels. Stored as theme JSONB on personas table. LayoutConfig interface and LAYOUT_PRESETS constants drive rendering.

nodes.label: Full entry point map (unauth / auth / embedded / AI agent)
nodes.description: Unauthenticated: landing, public persona, shadow, claim, endorse. Authenticated: dashboard, personas, communities, coach, inbox, explore, recommend, profile, settings. AI agent: MCP tools surface.

nodes.label: Component library (EntityCard, PersonaCard, etc.)
nodes.description: Shared UI components: EntityCard, PersonaCard, EndorsementCard, ContactRequestCard, CompletenessIndicator, TierBadge, VerificationBadge. Design system: spacing scale, OKLCH typography, responsive breakpoints.

nodes.label: GAP: MCP endpoint has no authentication (P0)
nodes.description: apps/web/app/api/mcp/route.ts creates server per-request with zero auth. No OAuth 2.0 + PKCE, no Clerk session validation. Linear: PER-5. Minimum fix: add OAuth 2.0 or Clerk session validation.

nodes.label: GAP: Agent tools bypass ownership checks (P0)
nodes.description: persona-coach.ts queries personas by personaUri without userId filter. No principal parameter on any tool execute function. IDOR risk. Linear: PER-6. Fix: add principal parameter, filter by userId.

nodes.label: GAP: Cost caps declared but unenforced (P0)
nodes.description: Profile declares per_request_usd: 0.50, per_user_daily_usd: 10.00, per_agent_run_usd: 5.00. No maxSteps, no cost accumulator, no latency cap on any Mastra agent. Linear: PER-7.

nodes.label: GAP: Service functions do not receive a principal (P0)
nodes.description: Server actions call ensureUser() returning a userId string, not a Principal object. CASL abilities exist but defineAbilitiesFor() is never called from CRUD paths. Linear: PER-14.

nodes.label: GAP: No PII classification on schema (P0)
nodes.description: Zero data classification metadata on any schema table. Trait validation has no PII regex. Embeddings index free-text without PII gating. GDPR/CCPA requires per-field sensitivity classification. Linear: PER-13, PER-16, PER-18.

nodes.label: GAP: No rate limiting or timeouts anywhere (P0/P1)
nodes.description: No @upstash/ratelimit, no middleware, no statement_timeout on Neon connection, no LLM call timeout. Public cost-bearing endpoints (MCP, coach, search) completely unguarded. Linear: PER-19, PER-20.

nodes.label: GAP: No data retention policy or enforcement (P1)
nodes.description: No RetentionPolicy registry, no enforcement cron, no account-deletion cascade. activity_events, coach_sessions, query_logs accumulate indefinitely. GDPR requires purpose-bound retention. Linear: PER-25 + sub-issues.

nodes.label: Project snapshot (2026-04-10 onboarding report)
nodes.description: SPAIDE onboarding at 2026-04-10: Next.js 16.1.6, Turborepo 2.8, Bun, Drizzle 1.0-beta, 20 DB tables, 33 route pages, 13 schema files. Single commit (fb255e9) on main. 4 Mastra agents discovered.

nodes.label: Discovered actors (Visitor, User, Admin, agents)
nodes.description: Curated actor set: Visitor (anonymous), User (authenticated), Admin (control plane), ShadowClaimant (Visitor upgrading), PersonaCoach, RecommenderAgent, DiscoveryAgent (confirmed in code), CommunityCoach (in docs only — gap).

nodes.label: Missing ADR candidates (10+ decisions undocumented)
nodes.description: 10+ implicit architectural decisions without ADRs: Clerk auth, CASL, Drizzle 1.0-beta pinning, Mastra, pgvector, MCP server exposure, Turborepo + Bun, Tailwind v4, Biome, Vitest, next-intl (unused dep).

nodes.label: Public Benefit Corporation structure
nodes.description: Personus is a PBC with legally binding commitment: advance personal agency and economic dignity. Aligns with B Corp dimensions: governance, workers, community, environment, customers. Board has mission-alignment obligation.

nodes.label: Mission: personal data control plane for the agentic era
nodes.description: Personus enables personal agency in the agentic era. Structured, privacy-preserving digital identity that AI agents can discover, query, and interact with — all under sovereign user control.

nodes.label: The extraction economy problem
nodes.description: LinkedIn $17.1B/yr gating free profiles. Thumbtack selling leads to 3-5 providers. ZipRecruiter charging employers for free resumes. Nextdoor harvesting hyperlocal data for ads. Model breaks further with AI agents.

nodes.label: Growth flywheel (shadow personas → claims → endorsements)
nodes.description: User creates persona → endorses trusted people → shadow personas created for non-users → shadows discoverable by AI → found via search → claim invites sent → new users join → endorse their network → flywheel accelerates.

nodes.label: Social impact thesis (economic inclusion, community sovereignty, privacy as right)
nodes.description: Three mechanisms: (1) Economic inclusion via trust-backed discovery without pay-to-play. (2) Community sovereignty — communities own their data and intelligence. (3) Privacy as a right — enforced architecturally, not by policy.

nodes.label: Solo tier (Free + $12/mo Pro)
nodes.description: Free: 3 personas, 10 coach sessions/mo, 20 search queries/day, 5 intros/mo, unlimited endorsements and community creation. Pro $12/mo: 10 personas, 50 coach, 100 queries, 25 intros, skill demand intelligence, 2-hop trust chain.

nodes.label: Community Organizer tier ($99/yr Base + $199/mo Pro)
nodes.description: Attaches to individual communities, not users. Base $99/yr: 1000 members, 3 guild tiers, 5 offerings, broadcast routing only. Pro $199/mo: 10K members, unlimited tiers/offerings, all 4 routing modes, capability heat maps.

nodes.label: Pathfinder tier ($49/mo individual + $149/mo team of 5)
nodes.description: For systematic people discovery professionals (recruiters, BD, researchers). 200 queries/day, 3-hop trust chain, compound filters, pipeline tracking. Team: 500 queries/day, full trust graph, batch queries, ATS integration.

nodes.label: Enterprise tier ($499/mo Base + Custom Pro)
nodes.description: Up to 500 employees at Solo Pro. Unlimited communities and members. Internal talent marketplace, capability gap analysis, market benchmarking. SSO/SCIM, HRIS integration (Workday/BambooHR), ATS bidirectional, Slack/Teams bot.

nodes.label: Pricing principles (no gating, no data sales, no algorithmic pricing)
nodes.description: Six pricing commitments as PBC obligations: never charge for discovery, never sell user data, never use opaque algorithmic pricing, never lock into annual contracts with penalties, never degrade free tier, always share revenue with community leaders.

nodes.label: Sparks credit system (earned, not purchased)
nodes.description: Gamification mechanic: Sparks earned only through generosity actions (endorsements, shadow creation, welcomes, invites). Never purchased with money. Redeemable for temporary premium feature access. Visible social proof via badges.

nodes.label: Sparks earn mechanics (endorsements, shadows, invites, guild actions)
nodes.description: Core earn actions: endorse=5, detailed endorse=10, create shadow=8, respond to intro=5, invite who signs up=10, invite to community=5, welcome shadow claim=15 (highest). Tier multipliers: 1x free, 1.5x Pro, 2x CO/Enterprise.

nodes.label: Sparks spend mechanics (feature unlocks + permanent badges)
nodes.description: Temporary unlocks: +5 intros for 20 Sparks, +5 coach sessions for 25, trust-chain +1 hop for 15, community boost for 30. Permanent badges (at cumulative thresholds): Generous Connector, Trusted Voice, Community Builder, Guild Champion, Welcome Wagon.

nodes.label: Sparks anti-gaming measures
nodes.description: Diminishing returns on same-person repeat endorsements; 10-per-day cooldown; 5-shadow-per-day cooldown; reciprocal-only pattern detection; new accounts need 50% persona completeness before earning. Sparks cannot be purchased or monetized — fundamental protection.

nodes.label: LinkedIn competitive analysis (extraction benchmark)
nodes.description: $17.1B FY2024. Vulnerability: as AI agents route around paywalls via structured APIs, LinkedIn must choose between opening up (killing recruiter revenue) or restricting further (accelerating user frustration). Lesson: monetize services, not access.

nodes.label: Lead platform analysis (Thumbtack / Angi / Bark)
nodes.description: Sell same inquiry to 3-5 providers at $5-200 each. 80% of providers lose money per lead. Angi declining 10.5% YoY. FTC enforcement action. Lesson: guild routing is a membership feature, not a revenue model.

nodes.label: Community platform analysis (Circle.so / Mighty Networks)
nodes.description: Circle $27.7M ARR, Mighty $8.6M ARR. Limitation: each community is an island — no cross-community discovery. AI integration is basic (summarization). Personus advantage: every community member enriches the global trust network.

nodes.label: Bluesky / AT Protocol competitive position
nodes.description: $0 revenue, $700M valuation. Not designed for professional discovery. No MCP endpoint. Validates Personus approach: charge for services (intelligence, infrastructure), not access. AT Protocol portability prevents aggressive gating.

nodes.label: Emerging MCP economy (pricing norms being set now)
nodes.description: As of early 2026: Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, enterprise copilots all support MCP. Metering infrastructure emerging (Moesif, Nevermined, Masumi, Apache APISIX). Personus opportunity to set pricing norms for capability discovery via MCP.

nodes.label: Agentic Commerce Protocols (ACP, UCP, TAP, Agent Pay, AP2)
nodes.description: ACP (OpenAI/Stripe, live on Shopify), UCP (Google/Shopify/Mastercard/Visa), TAP (Visa, 100+ partners), Agent Pay (Mastercard/Cloudflare), AP2 (Google/PayPal). All need privacy-preserving identity layer — Personus commerce personas answer this.

nodes.label: Regulatory tailwinds (EU AI Act, eIDAS 2.0, GDPR, CPRA)
nodes.description: EU AI Act (Aug 2026): transparency in AI-mediated decisions. eIDAS 2.0 (Dec 2026): digital identity wallets with selective disclosure. European Data Act (Sep 2025): portability rights. CPRA ongoing. Privacy-by-design is a competitive advantage.

nodes.label: Defensible competitive moats
nodes.description: Five moats: (1) Trust network graph (cannot be scraped). (2) MCP-native first-mover. (3) Community lock-in (positive — skill taxonomy, tier history). (4) Regulatory moat (privacy-by-design). (5) Generosity flywheel (cultural moat).

nodes.label: Network Flywheel
nodes.rationale: Every network action (persona creation, endorsement, shadow creation, AI agent query, claim) is simultaneously a growth event, creating compounding user acquisition at near-zero CAC.

nodes.label: LLM Cost Trajectory
nodes.rationale: LLM inference costs declining ~80% since GPT-4 launch; projected 2027 cost $2-5/1M output tokens. Free tier becomes cheaper to support over time, improving free-user unit economics without model changes.

nodes.label: Auth Provider Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Clerk may not be right at scale due to pricing, data residency, DID support, and enterprise SSO requirements; AT Protocol has its own OAuth/identity graph. Abstraction allows swap via one env var plus new adapter, with no changes to server actions or route handlers.

nodes.label: no-pii-in-personas Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Personas are AI-discoverable endpoints; leaking PII would undermine the entire product promise. Non-negotiable architectural privacy guarantee.

nodes.label: ai-native-discoverability Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Product's primary consumer is AI agents; human UI is secondary. Silent HTML-only surfaces regress the core value proposition.

nodes.label: authz-at-service-layer Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Routes can be bypassed by internal callers, agents, and MCP tool exposure. Service-layer enforcement is the only layer that catches every call site.

nodes.label: mobile-first-ui Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Primary acquisition path is someone tapping a persona/community link on their phone from a Discord/Telegram/WhatsApp chat. A desktop-first surface regresses the core acquisition loop.

nodes.label: ai-cost-and-loop-caps Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Agent loops without caps are the single most common AI production incident; runaway cost and runaway tool-use risk.

nodes.label: trust-through-endorsements-not-reviews Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Review systems produce adversarial dynamics (review bombing, retaliation, gaming) that destroy the trust graph. Positive-only endorsements are the core differentiator from LinkedIn, Angi, and Google ratings.

nodes.label: unified-entity-model-for-people-and-orgs Gate Principle
nodes.rationale: Separate organizations table would fragment search, halve network effects, and create a second-class citizen problem where organizations get lower discovery quality.

nodes.label: Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) Structure
nodes.rationale: PBC governance makes the non-extractive business model legally binding, creating structural differentiation that P&L-bound incumbents cannot credibly copy without destroying their revenue model.

nodes.label: Default Deny Authorization Policy
nodes.rationale: Nothing is visible or accessible by default; access exists only because the owner explicitly granted it. The system never infers or expands access beyond what was explicitly granted.

nodes.label: Single Service Layer Principle
nodes.rationale: Every new surface-layer function gets authz for free by calling the shared service layer. No surface-specific business logic permitted.

nodes.label: Turborepo + Bun Monorepo
nodes.rationale: Shared types, Zod validations, and CASL abilities used by every app; split-repo design would require private package registry or git submodules.

nodes.label: Traits-Are-Copied (Not Referenced) Invariant
nodes.rationale: Privacy via denormalization: persona snapshots do not reference back to the master trait pool, preserving unlinkability. Editing user_traits does not automatically update existing Personas.

nodes.label: North Star Metric (Trust-Backed Matches per Week)
Input Metrics Framework (Breadth x Depth x Frequency x Efficiency)
CASL Authorization Engine
nodes.rationale: Chosen for native TypeScript rule-based ownership model, defense-in-depth at service layer, AI-agent reuse of same authz checks, and TypeScript ergonomics. Oso rejected for Polar DSL tax; hand-rolled rejected for maintainability; Postgres RLS rejected as primary due to AI-agent bypass risk when using a service role.

nodes.label: pgvector Extension
nodes.rationale: Chosen over dedicated vector stores for SQL joinability with structured filters (visibility, consent, ownership), transactional consistency with row writes (same transaction), operational simplicity (one system), cost savings, and GDPR delete path. Pinecone/Weaviate/Qdrant rejected because they require two-hop fetches and a separate operational surface.

nodes.label: Mastra AI Agent Framework
nodes.rationale: Chosen for tool-calling to service layer, streaming UI ergonomics via Vercel AI SDK, MCP tool reuse, and TS-native ergonomics. Cost-cap enforcement is a project-level responsibility not solved by the framework. LangChain.js rejected for heavyweight Python-ported abstractions; OpenAI SDK alone rejected for provider lock-in and per-call plumbing reimplementation.

nodes.label: AI Cost Cap Enforcement
nodes.rationale: SPAIDE profile declares per_request_usd, per_user_daily_usd, and per_agent_run_usd caps. Framework hooks exist but project must add pre-call cost-estimator and post-call token accounting. Tracked as P1 follow-up.

nodes.label: Hybrid JSONB Traits Storage
nodes.rationale: Flexibility for AI-extracted data and privacy via denormalization. Normalized trait tables would require a join for every persona read and schema migrations for new trait types. JSONB trades query-time type safety for flexibility; the trait_metadata system provides runtime type safety.

nodes.label: Trait Metadata System
nodes.rationale: The trait_metadata table controls display and edit config per trait type. No hardcoded components per trait type — adding a new trait type is a seed-data change, not a code change.

nodes.label: Persona Layout Presets
nodes.rationale: Five presets (Professional, Personal, Community, Service, Creative) control information architecture. Themes control visual identity. Keeping them separate lets users mix and match any preset with any theme.

nodes.label: Persona Completeness Scoring
nodes.rationale: Nine weighted dimensions allow the Coach to make specific gap suggestions rather than a single generic percentage.

nodes.label: Shadow Persona
nodes.rationale: Shadows are community-scoped and carry community membership through the claim flow. On claim, the user inherits both persona traits AND community membership.

nodes.label: Persona Embedding Generation
nodes.rationale: generatePersonaEmbedding() concatenates structured traits into prose then runs text-embedding-3-small. This gives semantic search meaningful signal from trait fields that would otherwise be invisible to a vector model.

nodes.label: Biome Linter and Formatter
nodes.rationale: Biome chosen for single-tool lint+format velocity, Rust-engine CI speed, and zero-config defaults matching project preferences. Prettier retained only for Tailwind class sorting (Biome gap). ESLint+Prettier rejected for speed and config overhead. Biome alone rejected for loss of deterministic Tailwind class ordering.

nodes.label: Data-Driven Community Types
nodes.rationale: Community types defined in seed data rather than code enums. Feature flags on community_types are the mechanism. Specs describe generic behavior and note type-specific divergence to avoid duplicating workflows.

nodes.label: Community Relationships Table
nodes.rationale: Replaces parentCommunityId self-referencing FK with a community_relationships table supporting four typed relationship types (chapter_of, affiliated_with, referral_partner, cohort_of). All relationships are opt-in.

nodes.label: Community Notices
nodes.rationale: Notices are short, time-bound, one-way posts (asks/offers) with no replies or threading. Prevents Personus from becoming a forum — conversation happens on Discord/Slack/Telegram.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Community Public Presence
nodes.rationale: Private (invisible), Discoverable (business card page), Full Profile (rich page + optional public directory). Simpler mental model than old two-toggle visibility approach.

nodes.label: Persona Context Membership (user, persona, community)
nodes.rationale: Every membership is (user, persona, community). This three-way relationship drives privacy, display, and scoped search. Membership must never be treated as just 'user in community'.

nodes.label: Vitest Test Framework
nodes.rationale: Chosen for TypeScript-native without transpile step, React+DOM support via @testing-library/react and jsdom, speed via esbuild, monorepo ergonomics, and Jest-compatible API. Jest rejected for ts-jest slowness; Node --test rejected for React/DOM DIY friction.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS v4
nodes.rationale: Tailwind v4 CSS-based configuration chosen for shadcn/ui compatibility, OKLCH wide-gamut color support, Rust-engine build speed, and single source of truth in globals.css. v3 rejected on greenfield as it would require a later migration; CSS Modules and vanilla-extract rejected for removing utility-first velocity and shadcn compatibility.

nodes.label: Monorepo Architecture (Turborepo + Bun)
nodes.rationale: Turborepo+Bun chosen for shared schema/types across apps with zero drift, fast install and hot-reload across package boundaries, content-hash caching for CI speed, and low tooling friction. JIT TypeScript packages remove build steps. Nx rejected for overhead at current scale; multi-repo rejected for drift risk on shared-schema systems.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM (1.0 beta)
nodes.rationale: Drizzle chosen for first-class pgvector/JSONB/Postgres enum support, edge/serverless compatibility with @neondatabase/serverless, SQL-like query builder, and generated inspectable SQL migrations. Running 1.0 beta accepted with exact build-hash pin in root overrides. Prisma rejected for edge issues and pgvector Unsupported escape hatch defeating type safety; Kysely rejected for no built-in migrations.

nodes.label: MCP Server Endpoint
nodes.rationale: MCP server chosen as AI-native discoverability endpoint reusing Mastra tool definitions. OAuth 2.1+PKCE is intended auth model but was unenforced at decision time (P0 gap). GraphQL and REST rejected as primary AI-agent surfaces due to weaker tool-discovery ergonomics and lower tool reuse with in-app agents.

nodes.label: Single Codebase Architecture
nodes.rationale: Mastra as a library inside Next.js rather than a separate service. Enables shared types, shared database connection, shared business logic, and a single Vercel deployment. Agents can call server actions directly without network round-trips.

nodes.label: Clerk Authentication Provider
nodes.rationale: Clerk chosen for hosted UX quality, Next.js 16 App Router first-class support (proxy.ts), generous b2c free tier, and prebuilt accessible components. Provider abstraction mitigates lock-in. WorkOS kept as exit ramp for b2b/SSO needs. Auth.js rejected for DIY burden on an identity-as-product application.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres
nodes.rationale: Neon chosen for native pgvector (critical for semantic search), best serverless Postgres performance (<100ms cold starts), database branching for PR isolation, pure Postgres (no vendor lock-in), and Vercel integration. Supabase rejected for bundling features already covered by specialized tools (Clerk, Cloudinary). PlanetScale rejected for MySQL, Turso rejected for SQLite — both lack pgvector.

hyperedges.label: Agentic Commerce Flow via MCP
hyperedges.description: AI agent reads Commerce Persona from Personus via MCP, applies per-category selective disclosure, and executes commerce transactions via ACP/UCP without exposing raw PII to merchants — the same selective projection architecture as professional personas

hyperedges.label: Composable Digital Identity for Personus Personas
hyperedges.description: EUDI professional credentials (as W3C VCs) layer with community endorsements and proof-of-personhood signals into an aggregate composable trust score displayed on Personus personas — modeled on the Human Passport stamp approach

hyperedges.label: Dual Federated Protocol Integration Strategy
hyperedges.description: Personus integrates with both Matrix (community communication layer, via Application Service API for activity observation and virtual persona users) and AT Protocol (public discovery layer, via App View indexed into pgvector) as complementary federated protocols serving different use cases

hyperedges.label: AIO Discovery Flow
hyperedges.rationale: All four components (schema.org JSON-LD, MCP tools, community feed API, llms.txt) are collectively required to implement the AIO (AI-Optimized Discovery) strategy. No single component alone achieves AI discoverability; the combination is the architectural decision. EXTRACTED.

hyperedges.label: Three-Part Membership Invariant
hyperedges.rationale: The concept (three-part invariant), the schema entity (CommunityMember composite key), and the governing spec together form an indivisible constraint: (userId, personaId, communityId) must never be collapsed. The spec declares the rule, the concept names it, the schema enforces it. EXTRACTED.

hyperedges.label: Community Closure Lifecycle
hyperedges.rationale: Community end-of-life requires coordination across the lifecycle spec (archive state machine), the closure spec (close flow + data export), the 30-day grace period concept, and the notifications spec (member notification during grace period). These four elements are jointly necessary for a complete closure experience. INFERRED.

hyperedges.label: Complete Bot Execution Flow (Mastra Channels)
hyperedges.description: The four nodes jointly define the complete bot execution flow: platform_channel_bindings stores per-community per-platform config, Mastra Channels routes incoming messages and auto-generates webhooks, asAgent() resolves principal delegation from the platform event, and the bot architecture's one-brain-many-mouths pattern orchestrates the final LLM call with identity never reaching the model.

hyperedges.label: Shadow Persona Viral Growth Loop
hyperedges.description: The four nodes constitute the complete viral growth mechanism: a community member endorses a non-user (creating a shadow persona), the shadow appears in the directory with accumulated endorsements, the claim flow at /claim/{token} converts the shadow into a real user, and endorsement transfer atomically migrates all social proof to the new real persona — incentivizing the non-user to join.

hyperedges.label: Trait Metadata Configuration Layer (DB-Driven, Admin-Editable)
hyperedges.description: These five nodes collectively implement the metadata-driven trait configuration layer: trait_metadata (41 rows) is the single source of truth, the rendering dispatcher reads displayConfig + editConfig from it, the admin UI edits safe properties without developer involvement, completeness_weight drives the scoring algorithm, and trait_taxonomies provides the controlled vocabulary for enumerated trait values.

hyperedges.label: Privacy Preservation Architecture
hyperedges.description: The set of constraints and features that collectively implement Personus's privacy-first identity model — unlinkability, visibility control, MCP gating, contact mediation, and PII separation

hyperedges.label: Public Persona Discovery Stack
hyperedges.description: All features that make a persona discoverable by humans, search engines, social platforms, and AI agents — SEO, structured data, AIO, OG images, and MCP tools

hyperedges.label: Metadata-Driven Trait System
hyperedges.description: The set of entities and components implementing metadata-driven trait rendering and editing — no hardcoded components per trait type; DB-driven display and edit configs

hyperedges.label: Consumer UX Design Research Bundle

hyperedges.label: Persona Lifecycle Management Stack
hyperedges.description: All features involved in creating, editing, and deleting personas — wizard, list, completeness scoring, deletion cascade, and trait divergence tracking

hyperedges.label: Trust network growth loop
hyperedges.description: Four nodes jointly constitute the trust network growth loop: shadow personas are created through endorsements, Sparks reward the act of creating them, and the flywheel mechanic depends on all three to convert non-users into users who then extend the network.

hyperedges.label: Privacy-by-design architecture
hyperedges.description: These four nodes collectively constitute Personus's privacy-by-design posture: visibility levels control access, commerce trait privacy tiers govern data exposure, regulatory tailwinds validate the approach, and the foundational principles mandate it.

hyperedges.label: AI-native capability discovery core
hyperedges.description: These nodes jointly power the AI-native capability discovery use case: embeddings enable semantic similarity, MCP exposes the query surface to agents, trust-weighted scoring ranks results by endorsement chain, and the Recommender Agent orchestrates the full flow.

hyperedges.label: Growth Flywheel Loop
hyperedges.description: Shadow personas, endorsements, Sparks, and the network flywheel together form the viral acquisition loop: endorse non-user → shadow created → AI agent discovers shadow → claim invite sent → user joins → re-endorses → Sparks reward generosity

hyperedges.label: Privacy-by-Default Architecture
hyperedges.description: The no-pii-in-personas principle, masked-contact principle, contact_requests table, and default-deny authorization policy together implement the product-wide privacy guarantee that no PII ever surfaces on personas and all contact is mediated
